items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: All three ACs have tests: a squash-only repo gets a pinned squash line and a merge-commit repo gets --merge (unit + real-git e2e through the gh stub); a moved base stops with a plain restart message and nothing is merged (e2e: PR still open, origin main unchanged); the guard, active, allows the chosen line (e2e) and denies the same pinned line once HEAD moved.

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: Every failure is a refusal with a reason and a plain detail, never a fallback to --merge: unreadable settings, no allowed method, unknown PR state, PR head or base mismatch, fetch or ancestry errors (base_state_unknown, distinct from base_moved which is exit 1 only).

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: Repository settings are only read; the head is always pinned; the push URL user and token are redacted from the answer (tested); the merge line carries only a git SHA and fixed words, never a stored URL or branch name.

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: 28 unit tests with an injected runner (each refusal, each method, CLI, SKILL template equals printed line) and 4 real-git e2e tests with a bare remote and the gh stub; the e2e asserts the guard is active so its allow is not vacuous.

items.name: Performance Basics
items.note: One gh pr view, one gh repo view, and for squash/rebase one fetch of the base; a merge commit needs no fetch. Only on the autonomous merge path.

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: Decision in a new 120-line lib/release_merge.py mirroring push-tag; fetch_base extracted from on_base with the same command keys; the gh stub split at its 300-line cap into gh_stub_support.py (now 267 + 76 lines).

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: gh repo view JSON (producer gh stub / real gh, consumer release_merge) and the printed merge line (producer merge-ready, consumers the release guard parser and the gh stub) round-tripped in the e2e: the printed line is parsed by the guard and executed by the stub.

items.name: Test Hygiene Probe
items.note: No skips, no .only; the new tests assert outcomes, not mocks.
